subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as an additive per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 remain the landing path?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but adding these per-agent config surfaces affects public config, provider/model routing, auth-profile selection, and session context behavior, which needs maintainer intent before another automated fix is queued.

options.title: Sponsor the per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the additive config direction and review or repair the open PR with deep-merge semantics, docs, tests, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` first and defer broader compaction and pruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only config
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the additive config direction and review or repair the open PR with deep-merge semantics, docs, tests, and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on per-agent defaults and the agent-scope config helper, where this history is strongest.
